project.purpose: Compose mature knowledge, capabilities, and project authorities into verified outcomes while remaining thinner than the systems it composes.

sharedCatalog.note: Used only for exact Agent/Harness/Runtime-related shared coordinates.

nodes.label: CapabilityCatalog
nodes.responsibility: Describe available mature capabilities and their natural authorities without absorbing their semantics.
nodes.replacementContract: Catalog/provider records remain replaceable projections over external owners.
acceptance: Capabilities can be discovered without redefining their external owner.

nodes.label: CompositionModel
nodes.responsibility: Compose task-local capabilities from a real problem through plan, act, and verify boundaries.
nodes.replacementContract: Composition method can evolve without changing provider/domain authorities.
acceptance: A composition identifies selected owners, effects, and verification boundaries.

nodes.label: AgentArchitectureCatalog
nodes.responsibility: Provide optional reusable LEGO coordinates for Agent architecture comparison and planning.
nodes.replacementContract: Catalog evolves only through evidence and Atomicity review.
acceptance: Core-24 graph references close and acceptance receipt passes.

nodes.label: LegoPlanningContract
nodes.responsibility: Project verified understanding into small nodes and bounded implementation slices without becoming project truth.
nodes.replacementContract: Projects consume the JSON contract; planning tooling may be replaced.
acceptance: R1 validator passes this repository plan and pilot project plans.
nodes.nextAction: Use R1 on future project planning updates; change the contract only from demonstrated planning failure.

nodes.label: ProjectRollout
nodes.responsibility: Adopt LEGO planning as a thin local projection across Ordivon owner repositories without forcing shared ontology.
nodes.authority: each project remains owner of its own plan
nodes.replacementContract: Each repository evolves project-native nodes independently while preserving R1 projection law.
acceptance: Each admitted core repository has a structurally valid project-native plan or an explicit deferred rollout reason.
nodes.nextAction: Adopt Workstation only after its current dirty worktree is clean and revalidated.

nodes.label: LegoQuestionCompiler
nodes.responsibility: Compile vague or overloaded problems into a bounded set of evidence-bound, decision-relevant questions before or between deeper analysis and planning.
nodes.replacementContract: The compiler may be replaced or refined without changing project/domain truth; downstream planning consumes only evidence-supported decisions.
acceptance: R1 keeps primary questions bounded, requires pruning and evidence/experiment handoff, adds no common Question schema, and passes repository regression.
nodes.nextAction: Prospectively test on at least two non-poker Ordivon domains before promoting any new shared LEGO concept.

edges.label: question framing hands sufficiently resolved work into evidence-bound LEGO planning

slices.objective: Freeze LEGO Project Planning R1 contract, schema, validator, and Skill.
acceptance: Validator accepts the canonical Ordivon-next plan and rejects broken references/evidence claims.

slices.objective: Roll out project-native LEGO plans to clean core repositories without changing their domain authorities.
acceptance: Each clean target repository has a validated planning/lego-plan-r1.json; dirty repositories are deferred rather than overwritten.
blockers: ordivon-workstation-v2 was intentionally deferred because its main worktree was dirty at R1 rollout time.

slices.objective: Add and verify LEGO Question Compiler R1 without expanding the common LEGO schema.
acceptance: Compiler Skill, method contract, and poker pilot exist; dedicated tests and full repository regression pass; no Question schema is introduced.

gaps: Cross-repository plan visualization is not implemented and is not required for R1.
No global priority scheduler is implied by project slices.
Cross-domain outcome improvement from LEGO Question Compiler is not yet established; R1 has one recorded poker pilot.

review.notes: LEGO Project Planning R1 remains stable. Question Compiler R1 is a verified experimental cross-cutting analysis lens with one poker pilot; it routes eligible turning-point/deep-uncertainty questions to lego-regime-shift. Cross-domain outcome improvement remains unproven.
